source.snippet: I've noticed the same failure mode across most coding agents. When an implementation runs into a problem, such as a function not meeting the requirement, the agent often writes a replacement. If the overall approach changes, it starts a new path. If only a detail needs adjustment, it may add another helper or class. What it rarely does is remove the code and data definitions added for the abandoned approach. After a few iterations, the result may work, but it contains stale branches, unused definitions, and dead imports.

problem_statement: AI coding agents accumulate dead code, stale branches, and unused definitions when changing implementation direction, leaving codebases progressively harder to maintain and audit even when the final output works.
target_segment: Software developers and engineering teams using AI coding agents (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, etc.) in professional/commercial projects.
notes: Fresh signal (2026-09-16), 3 points with comments, author describes a clear recurring failure mode across 'most coding agents' — implies broad experience with paid tools. Buyer context: professional devs paying for agent subscriptions (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, etc.). Opportunity: a post-agent cleanup tool or agent wrapper that diffs and prunes abandoned code paths. Could be a CLI, IDE extension, or agent plugin. Willingness-to-pay evidence is indirect but implied by the professional context and frustration with multiple paid tools.
